# Veneer: Full Technical & Plain-English Reference for AI Agents

> Notes that look like ordinary notes. Hide your real notes, titles, and images behind an everyday cover note in Obsidian. Type `;;` and your password on any line to reveal.

---

## 1. Plain-English Overview: How Veneer Works

Most encryption tools announce themselves. A file named `passwords.md.enc`, a padlock icon in the sidebar, or a modal prompt asking `"Enter Master Password to Decrypt"` immediately tells anyone looking at your screen or syncing your folder that you are hiding something important.

Veneer takes the opposite approach: **screen-level plausible deniability**.

1. **Ordinary Markdown on Disk**: A protected note is stored as a normal `.md` file named after its decoy cover, for example `Grocery run (Saturday).md`. Its visible body is a mundane, believable note such as a shopping list, standup notes, or a recipe.
2. **Hidden Frontmatter Envelope**: Your real note text, your real note title (such as `Q4 Acquisition Targets`), and any local images embedded in the note are encrypted using AES-256-GCM and stored inside an innocuous-looking YAML frontmatter property named `draft_cache`.
3. **Zero UI Tells**: Obsidian's Reading view hides frontmatter properties or displays them as standard metadata. Obsidian's global search, quick switcher, backlinks, and graph view index only the decoy cover text and decoy filename.
4. **Silent Inline Unlock (`;;`)**: There is no unlock button or password dialog. To reveal your real note, click at the start of any line in the editor and type `;;` followed by your password and Space or Enter. Your keystrokes are swallowed in memory so they never appear on screen. Within ~300ms, the editor swaps the cover title and cover body for your real title, real text, and decrypted images in RAM.
5. **Automatic Snap-Back to Cover**: When you switch windows (`Alt+Tab`), switch tabs, lock your screen, press the panic shortcut (`Ctrl+Shift+X`), or leave the keyboard idle for 60 seconds, Veneer immediately swaps the decoy cover back into the editor, wipes the CodeMirror undo history, revokes temporary image `blob:` URLs, and clears any text you copied to the clipboard while unlocked.

---

## 2. Inline `;;` Unlock & Blind Capture State Machine

Veneer intercepts password entry inside CodeMirror 6 using a highest-precedence `EditorState.transactionFilter` before any character reaches the document buffer, DOM, or Obsidian's disk auto-save pipeline.

### How the Capture Filter Operates

- **Trigger Prefix (`;;`)**: When the cursor is at column 0 of any line and the user types a first `;`, the filter allows it normally. When the second `;` is typed immediately after, the filter deletes the first `;` and transitions the editor session into `CAPTURING` mode.
- **Blind Password Entry**: While in `CAPTURING` mode, every printable character typed by the user is appended to an in-memory byte buffer (`Uint8Array`) and dropped from the CodeMirror transaction. Nothing is rendered on screen, so someone watching over your shoulder sees no password dots or prompt.
- **Backspace and Escape**: Pressing `Backspace` removes the last byte from the capture buffer (or exits capture mode if the buffer is empty). Pressing `Escape` or moving the cursor away aborts capture mode and zeros the buffer.
- **Submission (`Space` or `Enter`)**: Pressing `Space` or `Enter` finalizes the buffer and passes the captured bytes to the Argon2id key derivation worker.
- **Zero-Tell Failure Handling**: If the password does not authenticate the AES-256-GCM tag, Veneer does nothing visible. There is no error toast, no red border, and no shake animation. Failed attempts are rate-limited in memory using exponential backoff (`1s -> 2s -> 4s -> 8s -> 30s max`) to prevent automated keystroke brute-forcing.

---

## 3. Real Title + Image Encryption & Cryptographic Envelope

Veneer uses envelope encryption with authenticated AEAD primitives so that password rotation is instant and ciphertext size does not leak the exact length of a short secret note.

### Cryptographic Primitives

- **Key Derivation (KEK)**: Argon2id (`memory: 64 MB`, `iterations: 3`, `parallelism: 1`, `hashLength: 32 bytes`, 16-byte random salt per note) derives a 256-bit Key Encryption Key (KEK) from the user's password.
- **Data Encryption (DEK)**: Each protected note generates a random 256-bit Data Encryption Key (DEK) and 96-bit IV. The DEK is wrapped by the KEK using AES-256-GCM. Changing a note's password only re-wraps the 32-byte DEK without re-encrypting the entire note payload.
- **4KB Block Padding**: Before encryption, the plaintext bundle (real Markdown body + real note title + binary image attachments) is padded to a multiple of 4,096 bytes.
- **File-Size Matching**: To prevent an observer from noticing a 5-line grocery list that takes up 40KB on disk, Veneer pads the decoy text with proportional invisible whitespace and scales cover generation length to match the protected payload.

### Real Title Swap

- When a note is protected, Veneer extracts the cover's first heading (for example, `Grocery run (Saturday)`) and renames the file on disk to `Grocery run (Saturday).md` while encrypting the original title (`Q4 Acquisition Targets`) inside the payload.
- While unlocked in RAM, Veneer patches Obsidian's inline title element and tab header to display the decrypted real title. Every edits-to-save cycle writes the encrypted real title and real body back into `draft_cache` while keeping the disk filename and visible disk body fixed as the decoy cover.
- As soon as the note masks, the inline title and tab header revert to the cover title.

### Automatic Vault Image Encryption & RAM `blob:` Rendering

- When protecting or saving an unlocked note, Veneer scans the real Markdown for embedded local vault images (`![[diagram.png]]` or `![](assets/photo.jpg)`).
- Each local image file is read as raw binary bytes, packed into the encrypted AES-256-GCM payload inside `draft_cache`, and **unlinked (deleted) from the vault folder on disk** so unencrypted image files never sit exposed in the filesystem.
- While the note is unlocked, Veneer materializes decrypted image bytes into temporary in-memory `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` references and rewrites image `src` attributes in the live editor DOM.
- When the note re-masks, every `blob:` URL is immediately revoked via `URL.revokeObjectURL` and the binary buffers are zeroed.
- If the user permanently runs **Unprotect this note**, Veneer writes the original image files back to the vault folder and restores standard Markdown links.

---

## 4. Local Vulkan + WASM Decoy Generation

Veneer generates realistic, human-sounding cover notes entirely on-device so your persona, interests, and note metadata never touch an external API.

### Dual-Engine Local Inference

1. **Native GPU Acceleration (`llama-server` Vulkan)**: On Windows systems with compatible GPUs, Veneer launches a bundled local `llama-server` Vulkan subprocess bound strictly to `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port. This delivers ~135.5 tokens/sec on an laptop RTX 4050, generating a 500-word multi-section decoy note in roughly 4 seconds.
2. **Automatic WebAssembly Fallback (`wllama`)**: If no GPU binary is available or the user prefers pure in-process execution, Veneer falls back automatically to `@wllama/wllama` running single-threaded WebAssembly inside Electron.
3. **12 Instant Built-In Templates**: Works with zero model download required. Includes realistic templates for grocery lists, meeting notes, code debugging logs, workout logs, reading lists, travel checklists, and weekend errands.

### Supported Local Models & Download Engine

- **Built-In Model Catalog**:
  - `Qwen3 0.6B` (~378 MB, default ultra-fast model)
  - `Qwen3 1.7B` (~1.1 GB, balanced prose quality)
  - `Qwen3 4B` (~2.6 GB, rich multi-section technical and creative covers)
  - `Phi-4 Mini` (high-density professional notes)
- **Custom GGUF Support**: Users can paste any Hugging Face `.gguf` URL or import a local `.gguf` file from disk, with automatic SHA-256 checksum verification against the Hugging Face API.
- **Resumable Downloads**: Chunked HTTP Range download engine with pause/resume across Obsidian restarts, live throughput calculation, and ETA display.

### Anti-Slop Quality Scoring & Persona Matching

- **16 Auto-Detected Professions**: Setting a cover persona (e.g., `"backend developer who plays cricket and cooks on weekends"`) steers Auto mode toward appropriate document genres (code snippets and incident logs for engineers, campaign copy for marketers, syllabus notes for students).
- **Human Noise Injection**: Prompts instruct the local model to write like a real person jotting quick personal notes: using shorthand (`w/`, `re:`, `fyi`, `tbd`), mixing short fragments with longer lines, leaving thoughts slightly unfinished, and avoiding polished essay structure.
- **Automated Quality Filter**: Every generated cover is scored locally before acceptance. Veneer rejects and regenerates outputs that contain AI cliches, em-dashes, PII patterns (emails, phone numbers, SSNs), unapproved proper names, low burstiness (uniform sentence lengths), or n-gram overlap with your real secret note.

---

## 5. Duress / Destruction PIN (`;;!`)

For high-risk situations where a user needs to permanently destroy all hidden notes on demand without opening menus or dialogs:

- **Separate Prefix (`;;!`)**: Configured in Settings > Veneer with a 4-8 digit numeric PIN. Because it requires the explicit `;;!` prefix at column 0 of any line, it cannot be triggered accidentally during normal `;;` password entry.
- **RAM-First Crypto-Shredding**:
  1. Immediately zeros all active in-memory DEKs, KEKs, capture buffers, and unlocked editor states.
  2. Iterates through every protected note in the vault registry and strips the `draft_cache` YAML frontmatter property from each file on disk.
  3. Overwrites each file on disk with pure, unpadded cover text so every note becomes an ordinary plaintext Markdown file containing only its decoy cover.
  4. Purges the protected-note registry and duress PIN hash from plugin settings.
- **Silent Execution**: On screen, triggering `;;!PIN` looks identical to typing into an ordinary note or a no-op failed unlock.

---

## 6. Threat Model & Forensic Limits

Veneer is designed around honest, explicit security boundaries. **Veneer protects against people inspecting your screen or vault, not forensic analysts imaging your drive.**

### What Veneer Defeats

- **Shoulder-Surfers**: An observer looking at your monitor sees only `Grocery run (Saturday).md` when locked, and never sees a password prompt during `;;` entry.
- **Casual Device Snooping**: A colleague, family member, or border official browsing your open Obsidian vault, searching notes, or inspecting the graph view sees only plausible everyday notes.
- **Laptop Snatch / Physical Theft**: Auto-masking fires immediately on window blur, lid close / power suspend, or 60 seconds of idle time, wiping undo history and clipboard contents.
- **Cloud Sync Inspection**: Dropbox, iCloud, OneDrive, Google Drive, and Obsidian Sync servers receive only the decoy Markdown text and the AES-256-GCM `draft_cache` frontmatter blob.
- **Screen Recording & AI Recall**: Optional Electron `setContentProtection(true)` blocks screenshots, screen-sharing software, and Windows Recall from capturing the Obsidian window while any note is unlocked.

### What Veneer Does NOT Defeat (And How to Mitigate)

- **Disk-Level Forensics**: The presence of `.obsidian/plugins/deocy/` on disk proves that Veneer is installed, and YAML frontmatter containing `draft_cache` indicates which notes carry encrypted payloads.
  - *Mitigation*: Run a portable installation of Obsidian inside a **VeraCrypt hidden volume** (a full step-by-step guide is built into Settings > Veneer).
- **Cloud Version History of Previously Plaintext Notes**: If you write a secret note in plaintext while cloud sync is active and only protect it later, the cloud provider's version history still holds the original plaintext snapshot.
  - *Mitigation*: Create a fresh note, protect it immediately with a cover before writing sensitive content, or purge cloud version history after deleting any old plaintext file.
- **Obsidian Core File Recovery Plugin**: Obsidian's built-in File Recovery plugin periodically saves unencrypted editor snapshots to disk.
  - *Mitigation*: Veneer's Hygiene Check enforces disabling Core File Recovery and **refuses to unlock protected notes** until File Recovery is turned off.
- **Untrusted Community Plugins**: All Obsidian plugins share the same Electron renderer process and can inspect active CodeMirror editor buffers while a note is unlocked.
  - *Mitigation*: Keep your community plugin list minimal and audited.
- **OS Swap, Hibernation, and Crash Dumps**: The operating system may page Electron RAM to `pagefile.sys` or `hiberfil.sys`.
  - *Mitigation*: Follow the in-app Hygiene Check to enable full-disk encryption (BitLocker / FileVault / LUKS), disable hibernation (`powercfg /h off`), and exclude your vault directory from OS search indexers.

---

## 7. CLI Build, Test & Installation Steps

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+ and npm
- Obsidian v1.5.0 or newer (Desktop: Windows, macOS, Linux)

### Build and Verify from Source

```bash
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/farizanjum/veener.git
cd veener

# 2. Install dependencies
npm install

# 3. Run strict TypeScript typechecking (zero suppressions)
npm run typecheck

# 4. Run the Vitest unit test suite
npm test

# 5. Build production bundle (outputs main.js and copies wllama WASM assets)
npm run build
```

### Install into an Obsidian Vault

1. Create the plugin directory inside your target vault:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p "<your-vault>/.obsidian/plugins/deocy"
   ```
2. Copy `main.js`, `manifest.json`, `styles.css`, and the `assets/` directory into `<your-vault>/.obsidian/plugins/deocy/`.
3. Open Obsidian, navigate to **Settings -> Community plugins**, reload plugins, and enable **Veneer**.
4. Navigate to **Settings -> Core plugins** and disable **File Recovery** (required by Veneer's safety gate before unlocking any note).
5. Open **Settings -> Veneer** to configure your cover persona, review the OS Hygiene Check, and optionally download a local GGUF model or set a Destruction PIN.

---

## 8. Repository Architecture Summary

```text
src/
  main.ts        Plugin lifecycle, command registration, MarkdownView hooks
  settings.ts    Settings schema, GGUF model catalog, active model resolution
  registry.ts    Protected-note metadata bookkeeping
  crypto/        Argon2id KEK derivation, AES-256-GCM DEK wrapping, 4KB padding, image bundle packing
  view/          Live MarkdownView title/body swap, save interception, RAM blob: image rendering
  capture/       CodeMirror 6 transactionFilter for blind ;; and ;;! inline capture
  lock/          60s idle timer, window blur, powerMonitor lock, clipboard wiper, setContentProtection
  decoy/         12 built-in cover templates, protection wizard, password entropy checker
  llm/           llama-server Vulkan runner, wllama WASM runtime, resumable downloader, quality scorer
  shred/         Duress PIN verification, RAM-first shred orchestrator, OS hygiene checker
  ui/            Settings tab, model download modal, live status bar indicator ((cover) vs (real))
test/            Vitest unit tests covering crypto, capture filter, backoff, LLM validation, and shredder
```
